root_cause.trajectory_summary: The agent located the provided template workbook (/root/data/test-rar.xlsx), downloaded the IMF “external-data.xlsx” commodity database, extracted the monthly gold price series (US$ per troy ounce), and wrote it into the template’s “Gold price” sheet (Turn 20). It then inserted Excel formulas for monthly log returns and 3M/12M volatility, and populated the “Answer” sheet Step 1–3 areas with formulas and links to the computed values (Turn 20). A first recalculation pass with LibreOffice surfaced widespread #NAME? errors (Turn 21) due to function compatibility, leading the agent to patch Step 1 and volatility formulas and remove a stray #N/A cell (Turns 23 and 26). After patching, recalculation reported zero errors (Turn 27), and the agent verified that Step 1 outputs, Step 2 values/exposures, and Step 3 total reserves and RaR values were being produced (Turn 28). The final workbook was saved as /root/output/rar_result.xlsx.

what_worked.item: Successfully identified and downloaded the IMF monthly commodity database (“external-data.xlsx”) and used it as the source for gold prices, evidenced by the saved file and subsequent extraction/usage in Turn 20.

Populated the “Gold price” sheet with numeric gold prices through 2025M9 and produced computed return/volatility outputs, evidenced by Turn 29 showing rows 425–430 with populated B–E values (e.g., 2025M9 price 3666.5236, 3M vol 4.8133, 12M vol 3.2591).

Inserted formulas/links in “Answer” and produced non-empty computed outputs after recalculation, evidenced by Turn 28 showing Step 1 values populated (C3=1.64485, C4=4.8133, C5=16.6738, C6=3.2591) and Step 3 RaR values populated.
Diagnosed and corrected formula evaluation errors: after replacing incompatible functions and clearing a #N/A cell (Turns 23 and 26), LibreOffice recalculation reported total_errors=0 (Turn 27).
Saved the resulting workbook to the required path, evidenced by “Wrote /root/output/rar_result.xlsx” (Turn 20) and subsequent modifications applied to the same file (Turns 23/26).

issue.evidence: LibreOffice recalculation returned 863 #NAME? errors affecting Answer (e.g., Answer!C3, C4, C5, C6, C13, etc.) and Gold price volatility formulas (Turn 21).
issue.cause: The agent wrote formulas using function names that LibreOffice in this environment did not recognize (notably NORM.S.INV and STDEV.S), causing widespread #NAME? evaluation failures until patched.

issue.evidence: The rolling summary states Value/Volume sheets were inspected only for the “first 9 columns” and found a limited set of 2025 non-empty countries (e.g., Value 2025: Belarus, Georgia; Volume 2025: Uzbekistan, Czechia, Slovakia, Latvia). In Turn 20, the agent hard-coded Step 2 countries to exactly ['Belarus','Georgia','Uzbekistan','Czechia','Slovakia','Latvia'] and mapped them to specific fixed columns (Value!D18, Value!F18, Volume!F18..I18) rather than scanning all columns for any other 2025 entries.
issue.cause: Incomplete data discovery risk: by not programmatically scanning the entire row/columns for all non-null 2025 entries across the full width of the Value/Volume sheets, the solution may omit additional eligible countries that exist beyond the initially inspected columns, which would make Step 2/3 incomplete relative to the instruction “Find all the countries that has 2025 gold reserves value data”.

issue.evidence: The agent cleared Volume!E15 (first conditionally if it equaled '#N/A', later unconditionally) to eliminate a recalculation error (Turns 23 and 26).
issue.cause: This fixes an error-state but may remove an intended template formula/value in that cell; the trace does not show validation that Volume!E15 was safe to blank without affecting required outputs.

root_cause.outcome_assessment: Core mechanics (gold series import, return/vol formulas, Answer computations, and error-free recalculation) are evidenced as working, but the trace does not confirm that Step 2 enumerated all countries with 2025 data across the full Value/Volume sheets, so completeness vs. the task requirement cannot be verified.
